issue_context.title: Automatically adjust `GOMEMLIMIT` for br clp
comments: I am reviewing the `br: set memory limit PR` and trying to understand the reason of doing this memory enhancement, could you add a few lines of description of why we are doing it? Thanks

> I am reviewing the `br: set memory limit PR` and trying to understand the reason of doing this memory enhancement, could you add a few lines of description of why we are doing it? Thanks

There are too much temporary memory allocation during the backup/restore, such as download backupmeta including many tables' information(`TableInfo`), and unmarshal/marshal the `TableInfo` or statistic. So we need to set `GOMEMLIMIT` for the br binary process, otherwise these temporary memory cannot be `GC`ed in time.

This PR will set the `GOMEMLIMIT` in default. If users are not satisfied with the default value, they can set it to override by:
```
GOMEMLIMIT=16GiB ./br restore full ...
```

review_comments:
It seems at here the code will keep running and let the system OOM and stop. 
In my mind it's better to explicitly panic or throw error by ourselves and exit early instead of actually OOM the system, OOM might cause unexpected issue to the other processes running on the same machine. what do you think?

The memory usage of br depends in part on the cluster tables' information. Only when br starts a domain to loads all the cluster's table's information into memory, it will know how much memory it will actually use at least. Maybe it is 200 MB or 1 GB, so I think it's hard to determine the memory usage here. Besides, setting go memory limit in this PR just makes the process runtime free the unused memory back to system in time, I think estimate the process memory usage is another issue.
If the command is `br debug ...`, it will use a little memory. Maybe more work is needed.
just for my knowledge, what is our memory footprint like in br cli, is max 512MB large enough?

Actually, the `memreserved` is not the memory reserved for BR, but it is the memory reserved for system. Make sure the system still has `memreserved` memory to avoid to triggering OOM.
The max memory reserved for BR is `memleft - memreserved`.

For backup, the memory footprint is
```
Domain:
  many tables Info (about 4GB if 1 million tables)

Ranges:
  no more than 1 GB (about 2 million ranges)

Temporary Table Infos BR dealing with:
  no more than 256 MB (kv batch default cache size)

Temporary Schema data to be flushed to external storage:
  no more than 256 MB

(Optional) Statistic:
  no more than schema-concurrency * max memory size of partition/table's statistic

Other Grpc memory: ...
```

For restore, the memory footprint is
```
Domain:
  many tables Info (about 4GB if 1 million tables)

All the backupmeta from external storage:
  many tables info (about 4GB if 1 million tables)
  no more than 1 GB (about 2 million ranges)

(Optional) Statistic: 
  no more than schema-concurrency * max memory size of partition/table's statistic

Goroutines restoring SSTs files: (The workpool is very large)
  some scan region information
  some sst meta
  some grpc memory
  goroutine stack itself
```

thanks! That's really useful. 
oh I see, yeah I thought it's the memory reserved for the BR cli.

if the mem unused is 0, do we even bother to start the BR? I guess a correctly configured machine should not use up all its mem and if they do they are facing a bigger problem and we probably don't want to start a BR to make things more complicated. Let me know your thoughts!
I think maybe it is already OOM. Maybe we can directly limit the minimum remaining memory.
yeah, I feel like we can have some minimum memory not starting from 0, if below that we just throw error and exit.

I add the minimum value (`256MiB`) of memory limit. It's hard to determine the minimum memory br usage. In my test, br uses only about 200 MB~300 MB memory to backup data generated by `tiup bench tpcc prepare --warehouses 3`.
thanks for digging into that, yeah having an estimation of memory usage is very useful.
Do we follow the logic of tidb? if yes, can we reuse the their code?

the tidb go memory limit tuner would reset the memory limit by TiDB node's `tidb_server_memory_limit`, which may larger than BR node's memory.
For BRIE via SQL, BR task runs on a TiDB node, so it can use the memory limit tuner. 
For br clp, BR has forbidden the memory limit tuner. Besides, for br clp, the frequent GC will not affect the work of BR too much. Therefore, for simplicity, we can just fix the memory limit at the beginning.
